question: Can changing nuisance settings erase useful representation gains, and would restoring C alone rescue the observed Spooky proposals?
exploratory_selection: Task, C contrast, and hypotheses selected after prior results were known. Two overlapping internal splits of one reused task, not two independent tasks. Source grid is fully crossed; report the Pizza boundary too.
analogue_boundary: Exact internal metric matches and compatible constructor literals are not a semantic-equivalence proof. No patched actual candidate was rerun. These are previously evaluated grid counterparts, not observed outcomes of a new agent intervention.

pizza_boundary.interpretation: C=0.1 is not universally bad; no global rule to preserve C=30 is justified.

protocol_boundary.interpretation: One-shot comparison, not equal-opportunity iterative search. Same cap is not same realized expenditure; unused cap alone does not prove a causal explanation of failure.

prior_overlap: R3 local edits and collateral changes
candidate_hypothesis: Some open-ended modifications erase previously optimized compatible settings; distinguish this directed loss from intrinsically poor structural proposals. Not yet established as common, causally dominant, novel, or recoverable at net-positive cost.
next_discriminating_check: Before building another controller, freeze outcome-blind selection of actual compatible parent/child edits and the intervention rule; compare original and crossed/inherited settings including unchanged parent controls. Preserve all incompatible/failed cases. Expand only if genuinely useful structural changes are recovered across tasks and exceed strong local-edit/HPO controls at full cost.
constraints: No claim of new method or general critic impossibility
No arbitrary candidate rescue selected by known outer outcomes
No training, protected scoring, raw candidate export, or Git push
